Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Falcon 6X bought for President Mahama, not a retooling of Air Force – Abu Jinapor Source : Prince Adu-Owusu 17 November 2026 8:13pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, has rejected the government's explanation that the newly acquired Falcon 6X executive jet is part of a broader retooling programme for the Ghana Air Force.
According to him, the aircraft is a presidential jet acquired specifically for the use of President John Mahama, and should not be presented as an asset purchased primarily for the Air Force.
"This government has bought helicopters for the use of the President, which have been housed by the Ghana Air Force, a luxurious helicopter, which has cost the taxpayer a fortune for the Ghana Air Force to operate for the use of the President.
"This government has bought a 60 million United States dollars, 720 million Ghana cedis aircraft for the use of the President and is going to be maintained and operated by the Ghana Air Force. It is not a new retooling of the Ghana Air Force," he said.
Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Tuesday, November 17, Mr Jinapor disputed claims that the existing presidential aircraft was old and no longer fit for purpose.
He also challenged the suggestion that because presidential aircraft are maintained and operated by the Ghana Air Force, their acquisition should be regarded as part of the military's retooling programme.
He explained that successive governments, from the administrations of Ghana's first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, through those of General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong and former President Jerry John Rawlings, had relied on the Ghana Air Force to house, maintain and operate presidential aircraft.
According to him, this arrangement does not change the primary purpose of the aircraft or make it a general-purpose asset of the Air Force.
"The presidential jet is for the use of the President. So we bought a jet for the use of the President of Ghana, who today is President Mahama. If there's another President after him, he will use it.
So it is not for any Ghana Air Force, so that the impression is created that the Ghana Air Force has some plane which is being used for all manner of things and the President too can use it. It's a plane which is being bought for the use of the President. If somebody else is going to use it, it must be at the permission of the President," he added.
